title: Derived state has no auto-supersede: two concurrent fresh summaries of one shared subject both stay current
observation: Two writers racing to replace the same incumbent derived record (or commitment) could both succeed and leave two current records for one subject; the emulation conductor hid it by serializing writes per subject. Resolved in 1.28.0: a `supersedes` that names an already-closed commitment or derived record is refused with `conflict` (reason `supersede target already closed`) naming the record that is current for that subject, so the loser re-reads and supersedes that one; the writer that closed the incumbent itself (same derived id under a new key) is exempt and becomes an in-place update with no second superseded event.
evidence: test/state-binding.test.ts: race write with the stale incumbent → conflict naming v2; read shows exactly one current summary; same-id re-send under a new key → updated
emulation replay on 1.28 code: 3 Sofias, 36 shared-subject handoffs, 1 current summary per subject, contradictions 0
